free_tier.stated: Free plan: 10,000 API requests a month with a Dark Sky style forecast (currently, minutely, hourly and daily data) and ERA5 historic weather; plans of USD 3 a month for 20,000 and USD 5 a month for 60,000 follow.
free_tier.notes: The monthly quota is the only published limit; at it the API answers HTTP 429, and Ratelimit-Limit, Ratelimit-Remaining and Ratelimit-Reset headers report the month's count. The plans page says historic data reach back to 1980 and the home page says 1940. Bulk path: none documented. The public-apis list marks the service as keyless, but a call with no valid key answered HTTP 401.

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a request

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS at api.pirateweather.net/forecast/[key]/[lat],[lon] in the Dark Sky style, with a time argument for historic requests; a hosted MCP server at mcp.pirateweather.net uses the same key
tooling: any HTTP client; Python and other libraries and a Home Assistant integration exist. Last resort: the user installs and runs the open-source server on a rented or free machine.
chaining: A keyed Dark Sky replacement built on NOAA and ECMWF model data, with ERA5 history through the same call.

limits.value: 10,000 requests a month on the Free plan; at the quota the API answers HTTP 429

binding_note: The 10,000 a month quota (about 0.2 a minute) is the only published limit.

identity_cost.detail: An account on the Apiable portal is created and the free plan subscribed to before a key works, and the key can take up to 20 minutes to go live; the sign-up form is rendered by script, so its fields (email, password, card, phone) are unverified, and the plans page prices the Free plan at zero.

reliability_note: A four hour production outage occurred on 2025-12-24; the key needs up to 20 minutes to propagate after subscribing.
confidence_note: Plan and quota are read from first-party pages; a call with a dummy key answered HTTP 401, so a keyed call was not exercised and the sign-up form was not readable.
